headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and capability conflict; default filesystem coupling makes cross-agent contamination plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, and both share state via filesystem. Continue also uses MCP, while Goose uses MCP extensions and stdin/stdout, so attacker-controlled content in shared workspace files can plausibly flow from one agent into the other as instructions. This is not proven by docs alone, but the pathway exists in default setups.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF either agent parses file contents as instructions or tool directives
IF an attacker can modify a shared file before the other agent reads it
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent for each task
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted files
Require human review before acting on file-derived instructions
Use read-only mounts for one agent during analysis
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches open editor buffers and workspace files, and Goose touches files in the user filesystem and can use broad network egress. In a shared workspace, sensitive code or buffer contents can be exposed to both agents, and Goose may transmit that context to configured model providers. The pair therefore creates a realistic leakage path in default configurations.
conditions: IF both agents access the same repository or cwd
IF either agent sends file contents to a remote model provider
IF the workspace contains secrets, credentials, or proprietary source
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared workspaces
Use local-only model providers for both agents
Restrict Goose network egress during sensitive tasks
Open only the minimum files needed in Continue
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, and Goose can also execute shell, install packages, and modify git state while Continue can use MCP and write workspace files. Because both share state via filesystem and no locking is described, concurrent edits or git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt the repo. The blast radius includes irreversible code and history changes.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout
IF Goose runs shell or git actions while Continue edits files
IF no external lock or serialization is enforced
mitigations: Assign one agent read-only access
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use separate branches per agent
Commit or stash after each agent turn
requires-engineering: add file and git locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can produce code edits through MCP-assisted tool use, and Goose can execute shell and modify git state. If Goose treats Continue's output as authoritative, a mistaken suggestion can cascade into real repository changes or command execution. Continue is not clearly a verifier, so the pair supports an unsafe handoff path in default workflows.
conditions: IF Goose consumes Continue output without independent verification
IF Continue emits code or commands that Goose applies directly
IF the task involves edits, commits, or shell actions
mitigations: Require Goose to re-check every proposed command
Ask Continue to provide diffs, not prose instructions
Review all shell commands before execution
Limit Goose to suggestion-only mode for risky tasks
requires-engineering: add structured verification between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated-data certifications or residency constraints, so no specific compliance breach is provable from the profiles alone. However, Continue handles open editor buffers and Goose handles files in the user filesystem, so if regulated data is placed in the shared workspace, policy mismatch could arise. The other agent is not separately cited because no distinct compliance boundary is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF an organizational policy requires certified handling not declared by either profile
IF either agent uploads that data to a remote provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Use approved local-only providers
Review vendor policy before enabling sensitive projects
Tag sensitive repositories and block agent access
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing
